rv.q: At this first blush, Zimmerman is a bit stuck between period parody and contemporary reinterpretation and the show flits back and forth.
This miniaturized conception is charming, zany, fun and abundantly imaginative.
This is overall an inventive and purely fun execution of Zimmerman's vision for this MATCHBOX MAGIC FLUTE.
The results are nothing less than triumphant.
This Matchbox Magic Flute casts a far more powerful spell than many larger productions.
Her re-imagining of Mozart’s most famous and final work delivers an enchanting production that’s much more musical theatre than opera.
For patrons who don’t fancy themselves operagoers, or for anyone wishing to dabble in the genre, “The Matchbox Magic Flute” satisfies.
But that’s a minor point in this gem of a show.
Only here and there does it get its chin above the opera bar, and yet it is altogether delightful, a rambunctious good time.
Still, there’s no question that Zimmerman is onto something here that could really catch fire for smaller opera companies and children’s theater companies.
The Matchbox Magic Flute is utterly charming.
It is a fun production that amuses, delights and educates, all rolled into one.

cn.t: Critics praise Mary Zimmerman's inventive, scaled-down adaptation of Mozart's opera as whimsical, enchanting, and delightfully accessible, with reviewers celebrating its charm and playful reimagining for family audiences.
